name: Neck cream / retinoid for necklines
lead: Neck creams are topical cosmetic products marketed to improve lines, laxity, crepiness and pigmentation of neck and decolletage skin; some formulations contain retinoids or other active ingredients. They are a low-intensity option discussed among skincare-oriented appearance communities.

Published studies are small, mostly manufacturer-linked cosmetic trials. An 85-woman study of a comprehensive neck cream applied twice daily for three months assessed texture, fine lines, laxity and hydration [2], and a 16-week clinical study evaluated a firming cream containing N-acetyl glucosamine on neck and decolletage signs of aging [1]. Other reports include a nitric-oxide-enhancing neck cream [5], a randomized split-face/neck study of topical vitamin K2 (MK-7) [4], and a case of allergic contact dermatitis to a neck cream ingredient [3].
infobox: Retinoids, N-acetyl glucosamine, peptides, vitamin K2

paras: A 16-week clinical study examined a neck and decolletage cream with N-acetyl glucosamine and other ingredients for laxity, crepiness, deep lines and hyperpigmentation [1]. A study of 85 adult women aged 35 to 65 with Fitzpatrick skin types I to IV used a neck cream twice daily over three months with assessments at baseline and subsequent visits [2]. A 2023 report evaluated a cream developed to enhance nitric oxide availability in aging skin [5]. A 2026 randomized split-face/neck study examined topical menaquinone-7 alongside cell-based mechanistic work [4]. The abstracts available are product-specific, and independent comparisons between creams are not available in the sources reviewed.
A case report documented allergic contact dermatitis to ethylenediamine, a component of aminophylline, in a neck cream [3].

card.summary: Topical creams for neck lines and laxity; small product-specific studies report improvement in skin signs.
card.note: Studies are small and product-specific; contact allergy has been reported.

quick.overview:
Neck creams are cosmetic topicals, some containing retinoids or other actives, marketed for neck lines, laxity and pigmentation.

Published studies are small, product-specific trials of 12 to 16 weeks or so, reporting changes in skin appearance measures.
quick.mechanism: Ingredients such as retinoids, N-acetyl glucosamine or vitamin K2 are proposed to support skin matrix, hydration or cellular energy; the studies assess visible skin signs.
quick.risks: Irritation is a general concern for topicals, and a case of allergic contact dermatitis to an ingredient in a neck cream has been reported.
